description: Legacy Argus Array beta and rho curves (Niall Miller, 30 September 2026), with the samples his MESA projects read, unchanged: beta = Chroma CT446-162bp collimated design curve and rho = an idealised 560-825 nm box, each x a PlaneWave CDK optics model x Sony IMX455 QE, without atmosphere. Superseded by Argus/DR280.
short_description: Legacy Argus Array beta and rho curves, superseded by Argus/DR280
facility_description: The Argus Array, built at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, is an array of small telescopes designed to observe the entire accessible sky at high cadence (Law et al. 2022, PASP 134, 035003; Law et al. 2024, Proc. SPIE 13094, 130941W). The 2022 paper describes an earlier hardware design (g-band and wide g+r filters, IMX455 sensors, 203 mm f/2.8 telescopes) that has since been replaced; the current hardware is DR280 telescopes with IMX461 sensors and the beta and rho bands.
notes: Legacy curves: Nill's Argus beta and rho of 30 September 2026, which his MESA projects (MESA_ARGUS, argus_star, custom_colors) read. Their samples are served unchanged. On 27 October 2026 SED_Tools metadata (FilterID, DetectorType, DetectorTypeSource, WavelengthUnit, Components, ComponentsSource, Sources) was added to their column row, line 1, which released MESA discards, so MESA reads the same numbers; apart from line 1 they are byte-identical to the archived originals (source_evidence/filters/2026-10-27-argus/Argus_System_beta.dat and Argus_System_rho.dat). Detector type energy per the Argus team (N. Miller, 2026-10-27); argus_sim's throughput.py describes the product as a photon-rate response. Made with build_argus_filters.py (archived) from ArgusSim's argus_g.csv (Chroma CT446-162bp collimated design curve), bandpass_560_825nm.csv (an idealised 560-825 nm box, not the real rho filter), optics_throughput.csv (a PlaneWave CDK optics model, not the DR280) and imx455_qe.csv (Sony IMX455, standing in for the IMX461): PCHIP for the filters and optics, CubicSpline for the QE (extrapolated to 300 nm), on 10000 points from 300 to 1000 nm; no atmosphere. Rebuilding from those files reproduces both curves to 3e-8. Components (filter, optics, qe) are served beside them. Composing them uses linear interpolation without QE extrapolation, so filter x optics x qe differs from the published curves near the steep filter edges (by up to 0.072 in beta at 527.8 nm and 0.026 in rho at 561.7 nm; in-band rms 0.0034 and 0.0015), and the pivot wavelengths agree within 0.4 A. Inputs: argus_g.csv, bandpass_560_825nm.csv and imx455_qe.csv are public in argus-hdps/argus_sim at commit 785c92e8; optics_throughput.csv is only in the private argus-hdps/ArgusSim. All four, the build script and both curves are archived in source_evidence/filters/2026-10-27-argus on NJM (manifest.json gives each file's URL or origin, retrieval time and SHA-256). Credit: ArgusSim's CDK optics curve and the IMX455 digitisation are by Hank Corbett (UNC). The current hardware (Chroma CT699-259bp rho, DR280 optics) is Argus/DR280.
